headline: Advance Day Use Passes and Campsite Bookings for Alice Lake
reservation: Access often requires a free day-use pass during peak seasonal periods through the BC Parks booking system; check the official site for current activation dates. Camping reservations are distinct from day use and must be secured via the Discover Camping portal. During periods of high volume, the park may reach capacity early, necessitating a pre-obtained digital pass to enter.

days.title: Four Lakes and Highland Cedar Forests

stops.name: Four Lakes Trail
stops.detail: Hike the loop connecting Alice, Edith, Fawn, and Stump Lakes through second-growth forest and mossy basins.

stops.name: Alice Lake Waterfront
stops.detail: Utilize the swimming areas and non-motorized launch points for paddleboarding or swimming in the glacier-fed waters.

days.driving: Allow 15–30 minutes for transit; conditions vary based on Highway 99 traffic.
days.note: Trail conditions can be damp year-round; allow extra time for the Four Lakes loop if walking with children.

days.title: DeBeck Hill and Glacial Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Park Entrance

stops.name: DeBeck Hill Trail
stops.detail: Ascend the old logging road for a panoramic view of the Squamish River Valley and the Tantalus Range.

stops.name: Cheakamus River Path
stops.detail: Explore the lower elevation trails near the park boundary to view the rushing river and local birdlife.

days.driving: Internal park travel is minimal; allow 10 minutes between trailheads.
days.note: The climb to DeBeck Hill is steep; pace yourself based on heat and personal fitness levels.

days.title: Squamish River Valley Exploration
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from North Alice Lake

stops.name: Jack's Trail
stops.detail: Connect with the broader Squamish trail network for a longer excursion into the coastal rainforest.

stops.name: Stump Lake Loop
stops.detail: Complete a shorter, scenic perimeter walk ideal for spotting local amphibians and waterfowl.

days.driving: Local transfer only; parking may be limited at specific trailheads.
days.note: Check for local signage regarding trail maintenance or seasonal closures on the periphery of the park.

intel.title: Seasonal Day Use Passes
intel.text: Check BC Parks for the 'Day Use Pass' requirement which is often implemented from spring through autumn. Entry is not guaranteed without a digital reservation during these specific windows.

intel.title: Peak Capacity Management
intel.text: Parking lots at Alice Lake fill rapidly on weekends and holidays. Once capacity is reached, park staff may restrict further entry until spaces become available.

intel.title: Cellular Service Gaps
intel.text: Connectivity is generally stable near the park entrance but can drop significantly on the DeBeck Hill or backcountry trails. Download offline maps before departing Squamish.

intel.title: Squamish Supply Hub
intel.text: The town of Squamish serves as the primary location for fuel and electric vehicle charging. Ensure tanks are filled before heading into the Squamish Valley or Diamond Head areas.

intel.title: Early Arrival Benefits
intel.text: Arriving before 9 AM often provides a quieter experience on the Four Lakes Trail. Mid-day crowds are common near the main beach and picnic areas.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental vehicle at Vancouver International Airport (YVR) and drive north on the Sea-to-Sky Highway to Squamish for supplies.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are suitable for paved park roads; check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved forestry roads nearby.
plan.goldenHour: DeBeck Hill Summit offers expansive views of the Tantalus Range as the sun sets, though hiking down in twilight requires caution.
